body.x: UNIUNI Corp. (CEO Sooyeon Han) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9, as part of the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion.

UNIUNI is a deep-tech company that has developed and commercialized privacy-preserving spatial safety AI solutions. Using non-vision–based AI technology that detects falls, abnormal behavior, and emergencies without cameras or video recording, the company addresses safety issues in spaces where filming is restricted or sensitive, such as public restrooms, hospitals, senior care facilities, and public infrastructure.

Based on the philosophy of “safety that protects without seeing,” UNIUNI positions itself as a privacy-first AI company that balances technological innovation with personal data protection. The company has demonstrated its technological capabilities and innovation by winning two consecutive CES Innovation Awards from 2025 to 2026.

To date, UNIUNI has achieved milestones, including actual deployment and operation at domestic public facilities, selection for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups’ TIPS program, exports and local deployments in Japan, Malaysia, and Switzerland, and an AI performance F1 score of 0.9487.

At CES 2026, UNIUNI plans to showcase its Innovation Award–winning technology and verified export track record, while actively seeking global partners and buyers based on cases from countries where its solutions are already in use. Centering on privacy-protective AI technology, the company aims to accelerate entry into global smart city and public safety markets and to expand the international competitiveness of Korean technology as an Incheon–IFEZ-based company.

UNIUNI’s flagship solution, RestroomGuard Savvy, is a non-vision spatial perception AI solution that uses ToF (Time-of-Flight)–based 3D depth sensors and AI algorithms. Collecting no video or audio data fundamentally prevents illegal recording and privacy infringement. The company emphasized that the solution complies with domestic and international laws and policies related to personal data protection and filming restrictions.

body.x: Key features include real-time detection of falls, abnormal behavior, and emergencies, with automatic alerts, and an edge AI–based architecture that enables immediate, low-latency responses. The solution is designed to scale across restrooms, hospitals, senior care facilities, public facilities, and smart city environments.

UNIUNI is currently exporting its solution to Japan, Malaysia, and Switzerland, where it works with local partners and institutions to apply and verify the technology in real operational environments. Based on this hands-on export experience across countries, the company plans to gradually expand exports to Singapore, Southeast Asia, and major European markets.

Leveraging its CES 2026 Innovation Award, UNIUNI plans to accelerate its expansion into global public safety and smart city markets. The company will broaden proof-of-concept projects for public facilities and medical and senior care facilities, particularly in Japan and Southeast Asia, while also exploring a transition from hardware-combined models to an AI software–centric SaaS global business structure.

Looking ahead, UNIUNI plans to collaborate with overseas partners and local governments to build region-specific safety solution packages and, over the mid- to long-term, expand into European and North American markets, aiming to establish itself as a global standard for privacy-protective AI solutions.

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
